name: CoreWorkPermit
intent: Work permit management scaffold: a full app shell (CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar) with a single "Work Permits" sidebar entry, and a route header (PageContentHeader) carrying five tabs — Dashboard, Work Permits, Templates, Map and AI Agent (badged SOON) — plus a Settings gear as a far-right icon action. Templates is built out as the versioned template register — All/Draft/Published/Archived status tabs carrying their own counts, and a searchable, filterable DataTable with row selection, bulk delete and a New Template action in its toolbar, modelled on the Workforce Crews list. New Template and any row open the authoring page — the StateMachine widget in its work-permit variant, whose own shell supplies the Back button and hosts Discard / Save as draft / Save and publish on the far right. The other tab bodies are placeholders naming what belongs in them.
when: Starting the Work Permit product surface that owns its own app shell
A single-section app whose route content is organized by a peer tab set in the header
whenNot: A content page rendered inside an existing app shell -> use a content-only template
Authoring one permit's state machine -> use StateMachine, variant work-permit
A multi-section admin surface where the left nav switches content -> use Admin Panel

chooseOver.component: Assembling CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar + PageContentHeader by hand
chooseOver.because: Work Permit owns the shell and the route header, so permit surfaces plug straight in with the tab set and breadcrumb already agreed.
The two share a shell but not a tab set, and a fork would have carried Workforce's roster, settings sub-surface and ontology scope into a product that wants none of them.

allowedPlacement: route-level work permit surface that owns the full window

extracted: the Crews list shape — Filter-wrapped DataTable, row selection, bulk delete, row-action menu
project switcher and breadcrumb wiring in the top bar
tabbed route header with per-tab Empty placeholders
persisted active tab and project selection

lineage.confidence: unset — scaffold, no held-out eval yet
notes: Templates is the one live surface; the other tab bodies are placeholders on purpose.

Opening a template swaps the list for the StateMachine widget (variant work-permit) rather than a dialog or push panel: authoring a template is a place you go, not a panel over the list. The template does not own that surface — it is a caller, and Connect V3's process page is the other one.
New Template creates the draft ROW first and then opens it — a draft IS the unsaved state, so a new template that vanished on Back would be a dead end.
Edits apply live, so Discard restores a snapshot taken when the editor opened (or deletes the row, for a template created in that session) rather than declining to apply.
Publish REFUSES a graph that still fails L1-L7 and names the rules, rather than disabling the button — the same never-disable rule CreateProcessDialog follows.

Permit Templates mirrors the Workforce Crews list: a Filter-wrapped DataTable with search, column toggle, row selection and bulk delete, and no title band of its own — the create action sits in the table toolbar beside Columns, as it does in every other list here.

NO KPI row. The four cards printed total, published, drafts and archived; every one of those is the badge on a status tab three lines below, so the page opened by saying the same four things twice and spent a quarter of the viewport on it. The tabs carry the counts, and All is the fourth tab and the default — the register as a whole, which is what Total Templates used to answer.
Status switches the table rather than joining the Filters menu — a lifecycle, not a facet. Every count on the page derives from the same array the table renders.

Settings is the far-right icon ACTION, the way Safety Manager and Workforce both carry theirs — not a sixth tab. The tabs are the permit WORK; configuration is not one of those, and in the row it made the strip read as six peers when it is five and a lever. It still opens as a full body, and while it is open no tab is active, which is the honest state.
AI Agent carries a SOON badge rather than being disabled: the tab opens and says what is coming.
